title: Start with a conversation
summary: Before pregnancy, CDC recommends discussing your medical history, existing conditions and all medicines, supplements and vitamins with a healthcare professional. Bring your questions to that visit so the plan fits your circumstances.

title: Care that stays with you
summary: WHO recommends eight contacts with a healthcare provider during pregnancy. These contacts support checks, timely care and a positive experience. Ask your maternity team to help plan your own appointments and what each will cover.

title: A clear, flat sleep space
summary: CDC recommends placing babies on their backs for every sleep, on a firm, flat surface with a fitted sheet. Keep pillows, loose blankets and soft toys out of the sleep area. Room sharing is safer than bed sharing; weighted sleep products are not safe for infants.

title: Introducing foods with care
summary: WHO recommends introducing complementary foods from six months, while continuing breastfeeding up to two years or longer. Respond to hunger and fullness cues, prepare food hygienically, and gradually vary texture and variety. Discuss your baby’s feeding needs and circumstances with their clinician.
source_name: WHO — Infant and young child feeding

title: Make mealtimes a seated moment
summary: CDC advises keeping children upright and closely supervised while eating. Prepare food for their developmental abilities. Whole nuts, uncut grapes, popcorn, hard sweets and chunks of nut butter are among potential choking hazards. This list is not exhaustive; ask a healthcare professional about food preparation and choking first aid.

title: Movement across the day
summary: WHO recommends a variety of physical activities spread across the day for young children. Its guidance considers movement, time spent sitting and sleep together. Explore the age-specific guidance and discuss adaptations with your child’s care team when needed.
source_name: WHO — Activity, sedentary behaviour and sleep under five

title: Keep the card, plan the visit
summary: India’s Universal Immunisation Programme publishes a national vaccination schedule. Keep a record of vaccines already given and review the next visit with your vaccination provider. Some vaccines, such as Japanese encephalitis, apply only in endemic districts. Your provider can confirm local eligibility and any catch-up plan.
source_name: Government of India — Universal Immunisation Programme

title: Notice, remember, talk
summary: CDC milestones describe skills that at least 75% of children can do by a given age. The checklists are not developmental screening tests. Share observations with your clinician; speak with them promptly if a child loses skills or you have concerns.
